messages:
incidents-bot: [INCIDENT] High 5xx rate detected — service=model-proxy, region=us-east-1, symptom=gateway timeouts. Alert INC-4321 created. Paging oncall. https://redwood.incidents/INC-4321
Maya: I'm on it. seeing ~28% 5xx on /v1/generate, errors look like "upstream timeout" from model-proxy to backend-pool. Customers reporting slow responses.
Lee: Noted. Is this a capacity issue or upstream flakiness? Any pattern by model or client?
Maya: Quick grep shows spike concentrated on model=fastopt-v1 and routes with long seqs. Running a tail of proxy logs now:
```
kubectl logs -l app=model-proxy -n prod --since=5m | grep timeout | head
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] ERROR req=... upstream timeout to gpu-node-5
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] ERROR req=... upstream timeout to gpu-node-7
```
Jordan: Could be an upstream provider (bare-metal pool) having a networking hiccup. Can we route traffic to the fallback pool?
Maya: Yes. I'm starting an emergency routing change: set route policy for model-proxy in us-east to prefer fallback-pool. Command: `redwoodctl route set --service model-proxy --region us-east --priority fallback-pool --reason "5xx spike"`
Ravi: +1, meanwhile I'll bump autoscaling target for dedicated pools by 30% to absorb burst.
Lee: Reproduced: when routing to fallback-pool 5xx drops to ~2% quickly. Looks like a subset of GPU hosts had kernel-level network drops. We should keep fallback for the next 20m while we stabilize.
Maya: Notifying on-call rotation and customers via status page. Posting incident note to status: "Experiencing elevated 5xx due to upstream host networking. Traffic rerouted to fallback pool; mitigation in progress."
incidents-bot: [ACTION] Annotated alert INC-4321 as "mitigated by routing to fallback-pool".
Lee: From a monitoring perspective, two things to fix post-incident: 1) alert noise — current 5xx alert fires immediately on short windows and pages frequently, 2) missing dashboard to correlate upstream host metrics with API 5xx.
Maya: Agreed. During the incident the page was useful, but we had duplicate pages for every model shard. We should add grouping and a two-tier alert (warning -> page).
Jordan: Proposal for alert tuning:
- metric: rate of 5xx for /v1/generate aggregated by region
- warn threshold: 1.0% for 5m (notify #eng-sre but don't page)
- critical threshold: 5.0% for 3m (page oncall)
- suppress paging if root cause is known (i.e., routing in-flight) via alert annotation flag
Maya: Also set a short recovery window and a cooldown of 10m to avoid repeated pages during the same event.
Ravi: For the upstream provider failures, add a synthetic health check that runs a lightweight generate call against each GPU host and alert if >50% of hosts fail healthcheck for 2m. That would have surfaced host network problems earlier.
Lee: Good. We should also change the alert to include a runbook link and recommended mitigation steps (route to fallback, scale pool, file provider ticket).
Maya: I'll open a follow-up task: ROAD-1256 "Tune 5xx alerting and add upstream health dashboard" and assign owners.
incidents-bot: [NOTE] Created task ROAD-1256 and linked to INC-4321.
Jordan: Quick commands I used during mitigation (paste here for runbook):
```
# route traffic to fallback pool
redwoodctl route set --service model-proxy --region us-east --priority fallback-pool --reason "emergency mitigation"
# increase dedicated pool target
redwoodctl capacity scale --pool dedicated-us-east --delta +30% --reason "absorb spike"
# mute non-critical 5xx alerts for 15m
datadog monitor mute --id 12345 --duration 15m --scope region:us-east
```
Maya: After routing change and scale we saw steady state at ~1.6% 5xx and error logs shifted from upstream timeout to occasional transient errors. Customer impact reduced.
Lee: Post-incident tasks and owners:
- ROAD-1256 (Jordan): create dashboard correlating http_5xx, upstream host health, network errors, and routing changes.
- SRE-432 (Maya): update runbook with the exact redwoodctl commands and escalation steps.
- INFRA-211 (Ravi): open ticket with on-prem provider for host network instability and share logs.
- ALERTS-78 (Lee): implement two-tier alert and add cooldown/suppression behavior.
Maya: I'll schedule a short incident review with oncall and infra tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
Ravi: FYI I collected host-level pcap and sent to provider support, ticket SUP-998.
Lee: Before we close: let's keep the routing fallback live for 30m and monitor. If recovery holds, we'll revert routing and validate no regression.
Maya: Sounds good. Leaving a final note on the thread for runbook content and action items. Adding :thumbsup:.
incidents-bot: [RESOLVED] INC-4321 status changed to "stabilized" (mitigation active, follow-ups created).
